title: Stable prompt handoff & parameter guardrails for pinned releases
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Establish a machine- and human-readable contract that governs how a pinned model release accepts prompts, emits outputs, and exposes tunable parameters. The goal is to enable customers to safely upgrade to newer runtime builds and to allow Redwood to publish performance profiles without accidental behavioral drift for pinned versions. This ticket covers the spec, onboarding checklist, validation harness, and a small server-side enforcement shim for the control plane.
acceptance_criteria: A compact JSON contract format documented and versioned in the onboarding repo (max 2KB for typical models)
Runtime validates incoming request shapes for pinned releases and returns clear error codes for deprecated/unsupported fields
Published performance profile generation includes metadata linking to the exact contract version used to collect metrics
End-to-end test harness that runs 100 prompt fixtures against the pinned contract and flags deviations in output shape or parameter behavior
Design review and sign-off from PM and Design; at least two eng reviewers for the enforcement shim PR
plan: Draft JSON contract schema and mapping rules (this ticket)
Prototype validation shim in serving runtime that can be toggled per release
Add contract to model onboarding checklist and onboarding automation (CI job)
Generate a synthetic performance profile run tied to the contract and publish to model-catalog
Roll out enforcement in canary for a single pinned release, monitor, iterate
design_decisions: Use a lightweight JSON contract (no new DSL) so contracts can be embedded in model manifests
Separate 'shape' guarantees (prompt/response fields) from 'behavioral' notes (stochastic outputs, temperature semantics)
Validation is opt-in per pinned release to avoid breaking historical runs but enabled by default for new pins
Do not attempt to fully lock tokenizer semantics; instead record tokenizer version and map common tokenization differences in the harness
tradeoffs_and_risks: Strict shape validation reduces accidental downstream regressions but may break customers using nonstandard prompt wrappers
Making validation opt-in delays coverage for older pins
Embedding contracts in manifests increases manifest size but improves discoverability
Full behavioral guarantees (semantic equivalence) are infeasible; we restrict scope to structural and parameter semantics
implementation_notes: Contract fields: inputs.schema, outputs.schema, parameters.allowed, parameters.defaults, metadata.tokenizer_version, metadata.contract_version
Validation shim implemented as a middleware in the request pipeline that checks inputs.schema and allowed parameter keys
Errors return 400 with error codes: CONTRACT_SHAPE_MISMATCH, PARAMETER_NOT_ALLOWED, TOKENIZER_MISMATCH_HINT
CI job will run model-onboarding/harness with contract pinned and publish results to artifacts.redwood.internal/model-contracts/
Performance profile generator will attach contract_version to the published profile so dashboards can link back
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema matcher with edge cases (nested structured outputs, optional fields)
Integration test: run 100 canonical prompts from onboarding fixtures across pinned runtime canary and compare output shapes
Regression detection: add diff thresholds for token-level shape changes and parameter semantics (e.g., top_k ignored)
Load test: ensure validation shim adds <2ms median latency on 2048 token flows under continuous batching
open_questions: Should we support schema evolution rules (e.g., add optional fields) or require a new contract version for any change?
How permissive should parameter aliases be (e.g., temperature vs temp) to maintain UX vs strict guarantees?
Do we want to block model catalog publishes when contract tests fail, or allow with a warning?
